name: Zoho Vault
tagline: Zoho's cloud password manager for individuals and businesses, with team sharing, admin controls and SSO.
bestFor: Small businesses already using Zoho, Google Workspace or Microsoft 365
description: Zoho Vault stores passwords and passkeys with client-side AES-256 encryption and adds team sharing, user roles, access reports and SSO on paid plans. There is a free plan, and the paid Standard plan costs $0.90 per user per month billed annually ($1 billed monthly).
pros: Free plan includes unlimited passwords, passkeys, storage and devices
Standard plan costs $0.90 per user per month billed annually
Enterprise adds Active Directory provisioning, SSO for cloud apps, request-release access workflows and SIEM integration
Zoho's SOC 2 + HIPAA Type 2 report lists Zoho Vault among covered products
cons: Group management, folder sharing and breached password alerts start on Professional, which needs at least 5 users
No native Linux desktop app; Linux is supported only through the CLI and browser extensions
File attachments are capped at 2 MB each
freePlanDetails: Free Forever: unlimited passwords, passkeys and storage, unlimited devices, autofill, passwordless unlock, password generator, security dashboard, offline access, built-in 2FA authenticator, folders, mobile apps, browser extensions and desktop apps. Basic email-only support.
trial: 15-day free trial (Enterprise features, up to 5 users), no credit card required; the account moves to the Free plan if you don't upgrade.

plans.name: Free
plans.notes: Free forever; email-only support.

plans.name: Standard
plans.notes: Per user per month. Adds team password sharing, one-time sharing with third parties, TOTP sharing, passkey management, user roles, admin controls, IP restriction, Google Workspace/Microsoft 365 integration and priority support.

plans.name: Professional
plans.notes: Per user per month, minimum 5 users. Adds user groups, folder sharing, SecureForms (3 active forms per user), break-glass emergency access, 10 webhooks, CLI, breached password alerts, geolocation restriction, Azure and Google user sync.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Per user per month, minimum 5 users. Adds Active Directory integration, SSO for cloud apps, request-release workflow, Okta/OneLogin integration, help desk and SIEM integration, rebranding, unlimited webhooks.

plans.name: Flex
plans.notes: Custom volume-based pricing via sales, with tailored onboarding and extended trials for large deployments.

integrations: Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Azure AD, Okta, OneLogin, Active Directory/LDAP, SAML 2.0, help desk and SIEM tools, webhooks, CLI; Zoho Mail, Desk, Projects and Flow
compliance: SOC 2 + HIPAA Type 2 (Zoho report naming Zoho Vault)
support: Priority email, phone and remote assistance (paid plans)

name: Sticky Password
tagline: Czech password manager with cloud or local Wi-Fi sync and a lifetime licence option.
bestFor: Individuals who want local Wi-Fi sync or a one-time lifetime licence
description: Sticky Password stores passwords and passkeys, autofills logins and lets you sync through its cloud, over local Wi-Fi or manually offline. A free local-only version is available, Premium costs $29.99 per year, and a lifetime Premium licence is $79.99 one-time.
pros: Lifetime Premium licence for a one-time $79.99, including 1 year of Dark Web Monitoring
Choice of cloud sync, local Wi-Fi sync or manual offline sync
Premium and Teams include Dark Web Monitoring and breach alerts
30-day Premium trial with no credit card; Teams trial includes 5 seats
cons: Free version has no sync or backup across devices
No native Linux app; Linux and ChromeOS are supported only via Contactless Connect from a smartphone
Not open source and cannot be self-hosted
freePlanDetails: Sticky Password Free: core password management stays available on the local device, without cloud backup, multi-device sync or priority support. Accounts move to Free when the 30-day Premium trial or a Premium licence ends.
trial: 30-day free trial of Premium, no credit card (excludes Dark Web Monitoring); Teams trial is 30 days with 5 seats.

plans.name: Free
plans.notes: Local device only; no sync, cloud backup or priority support.

plans.name: Premium (1 year)
plans.notes: $29.99 per year for one user (shown against a struck-through $39.99). Includes Dark Web Monitoring for the subscription. No monthly billing.

plans.name: Premium Lifetime
plans.notes: One-time $79.99 (shown against a struck-through $199.99). Never expires; includes 1 year of Dark Web Monitoring ($12 value), renewable separately.

plans.name: Premium for teams
plans.notes: $29.99 per user per year. Adds an admin console; includes Dark Web Monitoring. Up to 100 seats can be ordered online; larger orders through support.

support: Priority support for Premium users (typically within 24 hours on workdays)

name: NordPass Business
tagline: Business edition of NordPass with an admin panel, shared folders, breach scanning and SSO.
bestFor: Small and mid-sized companies that want a low-cost managed password manager
description: NordPass Business is the business edition of the NordPass password manager, sold as Teams, Business and Enterprise plans with an organization admin panel, password policies and activity logs. Teams starts at $1.99 per user per month on a 1-year plan, sold only as a 10-user pack.
pros: Teams costs $1.99 per user per month on a 1-year plan ($1.79 on a 2-year plan)
Email masking, MFA, offline mode and Google Workspace SSO are included on every plan
Business and Enterprise users get a free personal Premium plan
14-day free Business trial with no credit card required
cons: Teams is sold only as a 10-user pack and lacks shared folders, password health and the Data Breach Scanner
Entra ID and Okta SSO and provisioning, Activity Log API and Splunk/Sentinel integrations are Enterprise only
Not open source and cannot be self-hosted
trial: 14-day free Business trial, no credit card required.

plans.name: Teams
plans.notes: Per user per month; sold only as a 10-user pack. 2-year plan: $1.79/user/month. Includes autofill, sharing, email masking, MFA, offline access, activity monitoring, Google Workspace SSO.

plans.name: Business
plans.notes: Per user per month, minimum 5 users. 2-year plan: $3.59/user/month. Adds group and folder sharing, password health, Data Breach Scanner for 1 domain, Vanta integration, free personal Premium for users.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Per user per month, minimum 5 users. 2-year plan: $5.39/user/month. Adds Sharing Hub, Entra ID and Okta SSO and provisioning, network allowlist, Activity Log API, Splunk and Microsoft Sentinel, breach scanning for up to 10 domains, dedicated customer success manager.

integrations: SSO with Google Workspace (all plans), Entra ID and Okta SSO and user/group provisioning (Enterprise); Vanta (Business+); Splunk and Microsoft Sentinel (Enterprise); CLI
compliance: SSO/SAML via Entra ID and Okta (Enterprise)

name: Psono
tagline: Open-source, self-hosted password manager for companies, with a hosted SaaS option.
bestFor: Companies that want to self-host an open-source password manager
description: Psono is an Apache-2.0 open-source password manager with client-side encryption that companies can run on their own servers or use as a hosted service. The Community Edition is free with unlimited users, the business edition is free up to 10 users, and larger companies pay $3 per user per month billed annually (minimum 25 users).
pros: Community Edition is free and open source with unlimited users, self-hosted or on the free hosted psono.pw
Business features (LDAP, SAML and OIDC SSO, audit logging, policies) are free for up to 10 users when self-hosted
Native desktop apps for Windows, macOS and Linux (AppImage, APT and RPM)
Stores and shares passkeys; includes SSH/RDP/VNC gateway on business editions
cons: Paid business editions are billed annually with a 25-user minimum
Professional support and SLAs are quote-only; standard plans get basic support
No email aliases, and the hosted business edition lists SAML and OIDC SSO but not LDAP
freePlanDetails: Self-hosted Community Edition: free, open source, unlimited users. Self-hosted business edition: free for up to 10 users with the complete feature set. Hosted Community edition at psono.pw: free, including hosting and updates.

plans.name: Community Edition (self-hosted)
plans.notes: Free and open source, unlimited users; password generator, sharing, MFA; basic support.

plans.name: Enterprise Edition, up to 10 users (self-hosted)
plans.notes: Free for up to 10 users with the complete business feature set: LDAP, SAML and OIDC SSO, audit logging, policies, compliance enforcement, SSH/RDP/VNC gateway.

plans.name: Enterprise Edition (self-hosted)
plans.notes: $3 per user per month, billed annually, minimum 25 users; purchased through sales. Extended support option quoted separately.

plans.name: SaaS Community
plans.notes: Community feature set hosted free at psono.pw, including hosting and updates.

plans.name: SaaS Business
plans.notes: $3.50 per user per month, billed annually, minimum 25 users; hosted business edition with SAML and OIDC SSO, audit logging, policies, gateway; purchased through sales.

integrations: LDAP, SAML and OIDC SSO; SSH/RDP/VNC gateway; API keys and callbacks; psono-ci command-line client

name: Passbolt
tagline: Open-source team password manager from Luxembourg, self-hosted or cloud-hosted in the EU.
bestFor: IT teams that want an open-source, self-hosted password manager for sharing credentials
description: Passbolt is an AGPLv3 open-source password manager built for teams, with granular sharing, groups, role-based access control and a browser-extension-based client. The self-hosted Community Edition is free, and Pro (self-hosted) or Cloud Business costs $4.90 per user per month billed annually, with a 10-user minimum.
pros: Community Edition is free, open source under AGPLv3, with unlimited users and instances
Pro adds LDAP/AD provisioning, SSO with Microsoft, Google, OpenID and AD FS, SCIM and account recovery
Cloud plans are hosted in the EU (Belgium/Germany, or Luxembourg on Sovereign)
Source code audited by Cure53 and a SOC 2 Type II audit completed in 2021
cons: Paid editions require at least 10 users
Passkey storage has not shipped; only WebAuthn as a login second factor (v5.17)
Desktop app is Windows only, and the web client needs the browser extension
freePlanDetails: Community Edition (self-hosted): free forever, unlimited users and instances, password and folder sharing, users and groups, RBAC, browser extensions, CLI and open API; community support only.

plans.name: Community (self-hosted)
plans.notes: Free, unlimited users; community support only.

plans.name: Pro (self-hosted)
plans.notes: Per user per month billed annually, minimum 10 users; volume discounts after 100 users. EUR price €4.50. Email support with next-business-day SLA. After expiry Pro keeps working but without updates or support.

plans.name: Enterprise (self-hosted)
plans.notes: Custom quote; unlimited users and instances, 4-hour business-hours SLA with phone, email and Slack support, HA/DR consulting.

plans.name: Cloud Business
plans.notes: Per user per month, minimum 10 users (EUR €5 monthly, €4.50 annual). Multi-tenant hosting in Belgium and Germany (GCP); email support, next-business-day SLA; 7-day free trial.

plans.name: Cloud Sovereign
plans.notes: Per user per month billed annually in advance, minimum 10 users (EUR €7); hosted in Luxembourg; adds LDAP/AD provisioning and action logs; bought through sales.

plans.name: Cloud Enterprise
plans.notes: Custom yearly quote; isolated container hosting in Luxembourg, custom domain and SSL, automated backups, phone and Slack support, 4-hour SLA.

integrations: LDAP/Active Directory provisioning, SSO with Microsoft, Google, OpenID and AD FS, SCIM, syslog output, CLI, open API
support: Email with next-business-day SLA (Pro, Cloud Business, Sovereign)
